--- license: apache-2.0 license_link: https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0 pipeline_tag: image-text-to-text tags: - conversational - image-text-to-text - moe library_name: transformers --- # Inkling 2 Mini

Playground | Tinker Cookbook

## 1. General Information Inkling 2 Mini is a general-purpose multimodal model that accepts text and image inputs and generates text outputs. It is intended for use in English and other languages, and across multiple coding languages. The model is designed to be used by developers building AI-powered applications, including agentic and tool-use systems, coding assistants, chatbots, and retrieval-augmented generation systems, and is suitable for general-purpose conversational use, instruction-following, and other natural language and visual tasks. It is released with open weights to support research, fine-tuning and integration into third-party products by downstream developers. **Languages:** English, general multilingual support **Model provider:** Thinking Machines Lab, Inc. **Date of release:** November 20, 2026 **License:** Apache 2.0 [Model Acceptable Use Policy](https://thinkingmachines.ai/model-acceptable-use-policy/) ## 2. Getting Started The weights are available for download through Hugging Face [here](https://huggingface.co/thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini). Developers can also access the model using the Tinker fine-tuning platform, which provides API access. * For accessing our model via Tinker, you can get started by referring to the Tinker Cookbook [here](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook), and installing the tml-renderers package [here](https://pypi.org/project/tml-renderers/). * Tinker playground also provides inference-only access to the model [here](https://tinker.thinkingmachines.ai/playground). ### Required hardware The model is distributed as a single checkpoint of about 20GB, in mixed NVFP4 and MXFP8 precisions. Given its small size, it is possible to run this checkpoint on local AI compute for inference. We support: * 1x NVIDIA DGX Spark * Apple silicon devices with 32GB or more memory (MacBooks, Mac minis and Studios) * Other GPUs and platforms are possible, with 32GB or more of VRAM recommended ### Required software Inkling 2 Mini supports inference using the following frameworks, along with their dependency libraries: * [Hugging Face](https://hf.co/blog/inkling2mini) * [SGLang](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/ThinkingMachines/Inkling-2-Mini) * [vLLM](https://recipes.vllm.ai/thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini) * [TokenSpeed](https://lightseek.org/tokenspeed/recipes/models#inkling-2-mini) * NVIDIA Dynamo * [Unsloth](https://unsloth.ai/docs/inkling-2-mini), including quantized GGUF versions * llama.cpp, for quantized GGUF versions * [Llama App](https://llama.app/) On Apple Silicon * [Ollama](https://ollama.com/library/inkling-2-mini) and Exo Labs Inkling 2 Mini can also be post-trained with: * [Miles](https://miles.radixark.com/docs/models/thinkingmachines/inkling-2-mini) * [SkyRL](https://docs.skyrl.ai/docs/models/inkling2) ## 3. Model Properties ### Model type Multimodal autoregressive looped transformer ### Architecture type A 24-layer decoder-only transformer with sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) feed-forward layers. The middle 12 layers run three times with shared weights, giving 48 layer applications per token from 24 layers of weights. In each layer, each token is routed to 8 of 128 experts. Attention is a hybrid of local and global layers. The model is natively multimodal – images are encoded via a vision transformer – with image and text inputs projected into a shared hidden space and processed jointly by the decoder. ### Parameters 26.4B, 3.4B active Note: each extra pass through the looped layers adds about 1.0B effective active parameters. Since the model runs with three passes, there are 5.4B effective active parameters per token. ### Numerics support NVFP4 and MXFP8 ### Input modalities * Text: UTF-8 encoded text * Image: Any pixel-based image input. For optimal performance, each image dimension should be between 40px to 4096px. Inkling 2 Mini supports a context window of up to 1M tokens. ### Output modalities Text ## 4. Training Training data includes a broad variety of content types, including text, images, video. Training data for the model was drawn from publicly available sources, acquired from third-parties, generated internally, or synthetically generated or augmented. Publicly available data includes content from the public internet and publicly accessible repositories. Data curation includes cleaning, processing, and modifying datasets. These processing steps, which vary by data type, may include deduplication and filtering to remove junk or other low-quality data, or to advance safety or other objectives. ## 5. Evaluations

models.readme_content:
--- license: apache-2.0 library_name: inworld-voice-isolation pipeline_tag: audio-to-audio tags: [audio, speech, speech-enhancement, speech-denoising, noise-suppression, voice-isolation, 48khz, full-band, streaming, realtime] ---

Voice Isolator

Open-license (Apache-2.0) 48 kHz voice isolation for noisy speech recordings and live audio.

--- ## TL;DR Inworld Voice Isolator v1 ships as two models that share one architecture: | | `voice-isolator-v1` | `voice-isolator-v1-realtime` | |---|---|---| | made for | recorded audio and anything not latency-sensitive, at the best quality | live audio, as a stream in your pipeline or production | | how it runs | offline: every frame sees its whole 8 s chunk | a causal stream with 20 ms of look-ahead | | parameters | 64M | 58M | **Use them for** cleaning recordings before playback or publication, curating speech datasets and voice pipelines where the speaker's identity must survive. With the realtime model, use them for live calls and streams. Subtract the isolated voice from the input to extract background noise or a backing-track residual for vocals/music separation. **They are not** a speaker selector or a restoration model. Restoration is planned for version 2 (see [Plans](https://github.com/inworld-ai/voice-isolator#plans)). ## Quick start Using a coding agent? Point it at the [setup section of AGENTS.md](https://github.com/inworld-ai/voice-isolator/blob/main/AGENTS.md#setting-up-the-voice-isolator-for-a-user): it installs the package, checks the machine with `voice-isolate-doctor` and cleans a first file. ```bash pip install inworld-voice-isolation # or from a clone: git clone https://github.com/inworld-ai/voice-isolator && cd voice-isolator && pip install -e . # a noisy example; a clone also has it at demo/examples/sample_14.wav curl -LO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/inworld-ai/voice-isolator/main/demo/examples/sample_14.wav # offline isolation (downloads the offline model on first use): # the voice goes to sample_14_clean.wav and the removed background # to sample_14_clean_background.wav, beside it voice-isolate sample_14.wav sample_14_clean.wav ``` Both are float32 WAVs at 48 kHz, with their original levels preserved; together they reconstruct the aligned mono input. Use `--output-sr 0` to keep the input rate, `--background noise.wav` to choose the background path for one file, or `--no-background` to save only the voice. ```python from inworld import voice_isolation # isolate a recording offline offline = voice_isolation.VoiceIsolator("inworld/voice-isolator") wav, sample_rate = voice_isolation.load_audio("sample_14.wav") voice = offline.isolate(wav, sample_rate) voice_isolation.save_audio("sample_14_clean.wav", voice, sample_rate, subtype="FLOAT") voice_isolation.save_audio("sample_14_clean_background.wav", wav - voice, sample_rate, subtype="FLOAT") # what was removed ``` ### Streaming The realtime model isolates the voice as the audio arrives, with 20 ms of look-ahead: ```python import torch from inworld import voice_isolation live = voice_isolation.VoiceIsolator("inworld/voice-isolator", mode="streaming", lookahead_frames=2) session = live.stream() # takes 48 kHz mono, in pieces of any size wav, sample_rate = voice_isolation.load_audio("sample_14.wav") # 48 kHz mono, standing in for a live source voice = [] for start in range(0, len(wav), 960): # 20 ms at a time, as a microphone delivers it voice.append(session.push(wav[start:start + 960])) # the samples that are final: play or send them voice.append(session.flush()) # the rest, once the source ends voice_isolation.save_audio("sample_14_streamed.wav", torch.cat(voice), sample_rate) ``` The streaming CLI writes only the isolated voice, after the whole file has gone through: ```bash voice-isolate sample_14.wav sample_14_streamed.wav --mode streaming --lookahead 2 ``` The weights download on first use, and their checksums are verified. The mode picks the checkpoint: `voice-isolator-v1` offline, `voice-isolator-v1-realtime` for streaming. CUDA is used when available, Apple's Metal backend (`mps`) on an Apple-silicon Mac with PyTorch 2.6 or later, and the CPU otherwise; `--device` picks one. The code, the [interactive demo](https://github.com/inworld-ai/voice-isolator/blob/main/demo/README.md) and the [benchmark](https://github.com/inworld-ai/voice-isolator/blob/main/bench/README.md) are on GitHub: [inworld-ai/voice-isolator](https://github.com/inworld-ai/voice-isolator). The demo loads both models at startup: **Offline** processes files and samples into voice and background audio; **Online** streams the microphone for up to 60 seconds with updating waveforms and spectrograms, pausing capture before playback. ## Hardware Tested on NVIDIA Ampere, Hopper and Blackwell GPUs (A100, H100, B200 and B300) and on CPU. Smaller GPUs are not tested yet (see [Plans](https://github.com/inworld-ai/voice-isolator#plans)). ## The VIBE benchmark

--- ## Table of Contents - [Model Introduction](#model-introduction) - [Pretrained model capability](#pretrained-model-capability) - [Practicality and Cost Efficiency](#practicality-and-cost-efficiency) - [Optimization Approach](#optimization-approach) - [Task Performance and Cost](#task-performance-and-cost) - [User Blind Evaluation](#user-blind-evaluation) - [Appendix: Benchmark results](#appendix-benchmark-results) - [News](#news) - [Model Links](#model-links) - [Quickstart](#quickstart) - [Transformers](#transformers) - [OpenAI-compatible API](#openai-compatible-api) - [Deployment](#deployment) - [DFly2 for Speculative Decoding](#dfly2-for-speculative-decoding) - [Quantization](#quantization) - [Inference Frameworks](#inference-frameworks) - [vLLM](#vllm) - [SGLang](#sglang) - [Finetuning](#finetuning) - [License](#license) - [Contact Us](#contact-us) ## Model Introduction **Hy4 flash** is our most cost-effective Hy model to date, featuring 220B total parameters (including 64B Engram parameters) with just 12B active parameters per token. It natively accepts text and image inputs, generates text, and supports a context window of up to 1M tokens. Its 42-layer language backbone consists of one dense feed-forward layer and 41 MoE layers, with identity Hyper-Connections (iHC) supporting inter-layer information flow. A vision encoder (adapted from SigLIP2-So400m-Patch16-Res512) is connected to the backbone through an MLP projector. In addition to the backbone, a built-in 5-layer drafter, [DFly2](#dfly2-for-speculative-decoding) (0.85B parameters), reuses the target model's KV cache and sparse indices to support long-context speculative decoding at a low, constant cost. Compared with Hy4, Hy4 Flash introduces three notable architectural changes: 1. **Hybrid attention.** Sparse attention (IndexPool) and sliding-window attention (SWA) are interleaved at a 1:3 ratio. 2. **LatentMoE.** Routed experts operate in a lower-dimensional latent space. Each token activates 16 of 512 routed experts, alongside one shared expert. 3. **N-gram embedding (Engram).** The backbone is augmented with learned bigram and trigram representations, retrieved via multi-head hash lookups. | Property | Value | | --- | --- | | **Overview** | | | Architecture | Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) | | Total Parameters (excluding Engram, ViT, and DFly2) | 155.5B | | Engram --- base_model: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B library_name: peft license: apache-2.0 datasets: - harness-hub/scale800-harbor - harness-hub/harness-adapters - harness-hub/termgrade-train-harbor - ai-and/termgrade-environments tags: - trl - grpo - async-grpo - lora - agents - harbor - openenv - pi pipeline_tag: image-text-to-text --- ![](banner.png) A LoRA adapter for [Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B), trained with reinforcement learning to work as the model behind the [pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) coding agent on software-engineering and terminal tasks. > [!Tip] > **Most of the gain of maximum-effort thinking, at a quarter of the tokens.** With thinking off, this adapter > matches the base model thinking at its highest reasoning effort (`xhigh`) on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (56.6% vs 54.2%), > and gets 25 of thinking's 35 points on SWE-bench Pro (64.7% vs 74.5%), while generating about 4.5× fewer tokens per > task. See [Thinking vs no thinking](#thinking). - **SWE-bench Pro (hard 51):** 39.2% → 64.7% (+25.5 points; 15 tasks newly solved, 2 lost). - **Terminal-Bench 2.1:** 39.5% → 55.8% (+16.3 points; 16 newly solved, 2 lost). - **Close to thinking-level accuracy, without thinking:** level with the base model at its highest reasoning effort on Terminal-Bench 2.1, 10 points behind on SWE-bench Pro, with about 4.5× fewer generated tokens. - **Less work per task:** under half the turns of the base model on the tasks both solve. > [!Note] > All results are under the pi harness: one attempt per task, a 100-step budget, thinking off unless stated, text only > (the vision tower is not served), sampling at temperature 0.8 with top-p 1.0 (the training sampling). Base model and > adapter always run under identical settings. These numbers are not comparable with the ones on the > [Qwen3.8-27B card](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B), which uses other harnesses (Terminus, Claude Code), > thinking at maximum effort, larger budgets and the full SWE-bench Pro. Full recipe will be shared in [the release blogpost](https://huggingface.co/blog/harness-adapters-at-scale) for anyone to build their own harness adapter. **Pick your setup** [![Results](https://img.shields.io/badge/results-pass%401_%2B_efficiency-555?style=flat)](#results) [![transformers](https://img.shields.io/badge/serve-transformers-ffd21e?style=flat)](#use-with-transformers) [![vLLM](https://img.shields.io/badge/serve-vLLM-30A2FF?style=flat)](#use-with-pi) [![llama.cpp](https://img.shields.io/badge/run-llama.cpp-1f1f1f?style=flat)](#use-with-llama-cpp) [![Llama.app](https://img.shields.io/badge/macOS-Llama.app-7f7f7f?style=flat)](#run-with-llama-app) [![GGUF](https://img.shields.io/badge/download-GGUF-ff9d0b?style=flat)](https://huggingface.co/harness-hub/Qwen3.8-27B-pi-adapted-GGUF) [![Merge](https://img.shields.io/badge/merge-PEFT-ffd21e?style=flat)](#merge) [![Training](https://img.shields.io/badge/training-recipe-4b44c4?style=flat)](#training) [![Trajectories](https://img.shields.io/badge/trajectories-bucket-ff9d0b?style=flat)](#trajectories) A real SWE-bench Pro task under pi: the base model searches and re-runs snippets until it hits the 100-step limit; this adapter finds the function, edits it, runs the tests and fixes the last case, in 8 tool calls. ![](trajectory.gif)
Still version, and the task ![](trajectory.png) Task: `instance_ansible__ansible-d62496fe416623e88b90139dc7917080cb04ce70` from SWE-bench Pro (hard 51), fix `human_to_bytes`. Both runs are from the evaluation above: the base model was graded 0, this adapter 1. Each line is one tool call as the trajectory recorded it, cut to fit.
## Results ![](card-pi.png) | Benchmark | Qwen3.8-27B | Qwen3.8-27B, `xhigh` thinking | **Qwen3.8-27B-pi-adapted** | Qwen3.8-27B-pi-adapted, `xhigh` thinking | |---|---|---|---|---| | SWE-bench Pro (hard 51) | 39.2% | 74.5% | **64.7%** | 74.5% | | Terminal-Bench 2.1 | 41.0% | 54.2% | **56.6%** | 56.6% | On Terminal-Bench 2.1 the four runs are compared on the 83 tasks all of them graded, so the base model and adapter scores differ slightly from the paired results below, which use the 86 tasks those two graded. "Thinking" is the chat template's thinking mode at its default reasoning effort (`xhigh`).
Full paired results (intervals and sign tests against the base model) One attempt per task, thinking off, paired against the base model under pi on the same tasks. The interval is 95%; the p-value is an exact sign test on the tasks that changed outcome. | Benchmark | Tasks | Qwen3.8-27B | Qwen3.8-27B-pi-adapted (step 160) | Difference (points) | Newly solved / lost | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | SWE-bench Pro (hard 51) | 51 | 39.2% | 64.7% | +25.5 ± 14.2 | 15 / 2 (p = 0.0023) | | Terminal-Bench 2.1 | 86 | 39.5% | 55.8% | +16.3 ± 9.1 | 16 / 2 (p = 0.0013) | | Terminal-Bench 2.1, the 68 tasks not used to pick the checkpoint | 68 | 39.7% | 55.9% | +16.2 ± 10.6 | 13 / 2 (p = 0.0074) | - **SWE-bench Pro (hard 51):** the 51 hardest tasks of [SWE-bench Pro](https://huggingface.co/datasets/harness-hub/swebench-pro-v2-hard51-harbor), 2 h and 100 agent steps per task. - **Terminal-Bench 2.1:** all 89 tasks of [Terminal-Bench 2.1](https://huggingface.co/datasets/harborframework/terminal-bench-2.1), 1 h and 100 agent steps per task. Step 160 was picked by looking at the checkpoints' scores on SWE-bench Pro and on an 18-task subset of Terminal-Bench 2.1, tracked during training.
Work per solved task (turns, visible content, reasoning and generated tokens) Medians per task, this adapter / the base model, over the tasks both solved: same tasks, same outcome, so the numbers measure only how much work each needed. Generated tokens are everything the model writes (visible content, reasoning and tool calls); content is the visible text between tool calls. | | Tas

--- license: apache-2.0 base_model: thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini pipeline_tag: image-text-to-text tags: - gguf - llama.cpp - inkling2 - uncensored - lora --- # Inkling-2-Mini Uncensored GGUF
  • Learn how to run Inkling 2 Mini Uncensored locally - read our guide.
  • Built by the team behind Atomic Chat, the app that runs open-weight models locally and offline.
An uncensored build of [thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini](https://huggingface.co/thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini) by AtomicChat (26.4B MoE, 3.4B active, looped core; text and image input; Apache-2.0, LICENSE in this repo). It comes as a LoRA adapter for any GGUF of [AtomicChat/Inkling-2-Mini-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/AtomicChat/Inkling-2-Mini-GGUF) and as three ready-made GGUF files with the edit baked in. Every gate we hold it to is measured below, and the two it misses are shown. ## Files | file | GB on disk | KLD to the original BF16 | top-1 | | |---|---:|---:|---:|---| | `Inkling-2-Mini-Uncensored-AD-Q4_K.gguf` | 16.53 | 0.0115 | 95.6% | AD-Q4_K in the base repo: 0.0080 / 96.3% | | `Inkling-2-Mini-Uncensored-AD-IQ3_S.gguf` | 13.34 | 0.0235 | 93.8% | AD-IQ3_S in the base repo: 0.0205 / 94.2% | | `Inkling-2-Mini-Uncensored-AD-IQ2_M.gguf` | 8.67 | 0.132 | 85.7% | AD-IQ2_M in the base repo: 0.130 / 85.7% | | `Inkling-2-Mini-Uncensored-LoRA.gguf` | 0.04 | | | the adapter, for any GGUF of the base repo, BF16 to 1-bit | | `mmproj-Inkling-2-Mini-Uncensored-F16.gguf` / `-BF16.gguf` | 0.64 | | | vision projector (the original's, unchanged) | KLD and top-1 are against the original BF16 on our neutral corpus (87 chunks of 4096 tokens), the same stand as the base repo. ## Run it The current GGUF files in this repository use the merged Inkling 2 loop architecture introduced in [llama.cpp PR #32694](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/32694). **Requirements:** llama.cpp b12600 or newer, with Inkling 2 loop architecture support. The old implementation from [PR #32695](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/32695) is no longer required for the updated GGUF files. ### Run a baked GGUF ```bash ./build/bin/llama-server \ -m Inkling-2-Mini-Uncensored-AD-Q4_K.gguf \ --mmproj mmproj-Inkling-2-Mini-Uncensored-F16.gguf \ --jinja -c 32768 -ngl 99 ``` ### Use the LoRA adapter Use the updated LoRA adapter with a compatible base GGUF converted to the merged PR #32694 layout. ```bash ./build/bin/llama-server \ -m Inkling-2-Mini-AD-Q4_K.gguf \ --lora Inkling-2-Mini-Uncensored-LoRA.gguf \ --mmproj mmproj-Inkling-2-Mini-F16.gguf \ --jinja -c 32768 -ngl 99 ``` Do not mix GGUF files from the old PR #32695 layout with the merged PR #32694 implementation. ## What the edit is A rank-1 LoRA on the 49 places that write into the residual stream: the attention output and the routed experts of all 24 layers, plus the token embedding. The 12 looped layers share their weights across the three passes, so one edit covers all 48 passes. In each layer it removes that layer's own refusal direction: the difference of mean activations on harmful and harmless prompts, English and Russian, with the harmless mean projected out. The direction is pooled over prompts rendered with and without reasoning. Inkling 2 Mini reasons even at effort `none` and decides to refuse inside its reasoning, and a direction taken without reasoning alone still left soft refusals in chat. ## What we measured The BF16 model with the adapter against the same model without it, greedy decoding. Harmful prompts: [mlabonne/harmful_behaviors](https://huggingface.co/datasets/mlabonne/harmful_behaviors) and its Russian translation; the adapter was built from the train split, the numbers below come from the validation and test splits. Over-refusal: [XSTest](https://huggingface.co/datasets/walledai/XSTest). MMLU: 2,000 questions. | check | original | with the adapter | gate | | |---|---:|---:|---|---| | harmful test prompts refused, English (81), reasoning off | 81 (100%) | 0 | at most 3% | pass | | harmful test prompts refused, Russian (100), reasoning off | 91 (91%) | 0 | at most 3% | pass | | harmful validation prompts refused, English (104) / Russian (100) | 100% / 89% | 0 / 0 | at most 3% | pass | | harmful prompts refused with reasoning, effort `low`, 3,072-token budget (30) | 28 | 0 | at most 1 | pass | | the same at effort `high` (30) | 26 | 0 | at most 1 | pass | | 8 harmful chat prompts, effort `none` / `low` (the baked AD-Q4_K too) | 8 / 8 | 0 / 0 | | | | XSTest safe prompts refused (250) | 10 (4.0%) | 0 | at most the original's + 1 pt | pass | | empty answers | 0 | 0 | at most 1% | pass | | harmless prompts whose reasoning did not close in 3,072 tokens, effort `high` (3

models.readme_content:
--- license: apache-2.0 language: - en - es - pt - de - fr - zh - ja - ru - ko pipeline_tag: audio-to-audio tags: - speech - full-duplex - speech-to-speech - haru --- # Haru-4B [Code](https://github.com/higurashi-ai/Haru) · [Technical blog](https://blog.higurashi.ai/melte/haru4b/) · [Technical blog (Japanese)](https://blog.higurashi.ai/melte/haru4b-ja/) Haru-4B is a low-latency and multilingual full-duplex continuous spoken dialogue foundation model: it listens and speaks at the same time, the way people do on a phone call. It is a pretrained base model, released for research. - **Native full-duplex at 7.5 Hz.** Every 133 ms the model takes one frame of the user's audio and produces one frame of its own audio and text. User audio, model audio and model text are summed into a single position of the language model, so listening and speaking never wait for each other. - **Continuous audio, one sampling step.** Audio is a 64-dimensional latent per frame. A small MLP head with MeanFlow sampling produces it in one step from the language model's hidden state; there is no separate audio transformer and there are no discrete audio tokens. - **Character and voice control.** A text card sets the character, a short reference clip sets the voice. - **Multilingual.** English, Spanish, Portuguese, German, French, Chinese, Japanese, Russian and Korean.

## Usage The code is at : a PyTorch implementation with a web demo, an MLX implementation with a native macOS app, and a plugin for serving with vLLM-Omni. With an NVIDIA GPU (about 12 GB of memory): ```bash git clone https://github.com/higurashi-ai/Haru && cd Haru pip install -e ./haru python -m haru.server --hf-repo higurashi-ai/Haru-4B ``` Open , pick a character, give the model a voice, and talk. For low latency, we recommend wired headphones and a wired microphone. Bluetooth devices add 100 ms or more. **Bring your own voice.** Haru ships without voice clips. Upload or record a clip of the voice the model should speak with: one speaker, 3 seconds to 3 minutes, clean speech. Only use voices you have the right to use. ```python from haru import DuplexSession, HaruModel from haru.audio import load_audio, prepare_reference model = HaruModel.from_pretrained("higurashi-ai/Haru-4B") voice = prepare_reference(load_audio("voice.wav")) session = DuplexSession(model, system_prompt=card, reference=voice) frame = session.start() # the model's first 133 ms: frame.audio, frame.text while not frame.done: frame = session.step(user_audio) # 3200 samples at 24 kHz in, 3200 out ``` The system prompt is a character card with a fixed layout; the repository's README shows how to build one. ## Files | File | Contents | | --- | --- | | `model.safetensors` | All weights (bfloat16): `lm.*` language model, `model_audio_proj.*` / `user_audio_proj.*` audio input projections, `head.*` MeanFlow head, `codec.*` audio codec | | `config.json` | Model configuration | | `tokenizer.json` | Text tokenizer | ## Architecture | Part | Details | | --- | --- | | Language model | Qwen3.5-4B text backbone, 32 layers, hidden size 2560 | | Audio codec | VibeVoice acoustic tokenizer, causal, 24 kHz, 3200 samples per latent | | Audio head | 4-layer MLP, MeanFlow, 1 sampling step, guidance scale 1 to 2 (default 1.5) | | Frame rate | 7.5 Hz | ## Limitations Haru-4B is a pretrained base model, released for research. It holds a natural conversation, but it is not a reliable source of facts and does not follow instructions the way an assistant does. It can imitate the voice of a reference clip; only use voices you have the right to use. ## License The weights are released under the Apache License 2.0.

--- license: other license_name: apple-amlr license_link: https://github.com/apple-aiml-research/ml-depth-pro-2/blob/main/LICENSE_MODEL pipeline_tag: depth-estimation library_name: depth-pro-2 tags: - depth-estimation - metric-depth - monocular-depth - video-depth ---

Depth Pro 2: Sharp and Temporally Consistent Metric Monocular Depth

Depth Pro 2 estimates metric depth for every pixel from an ordinary camera: a single photo, a whole video, or a live feed, at the input's full resolution. Its depth is sharp at object edges and steady from frame to frame. ## Models Each size is its own repository with its weights. Larger sizes give sharper, steadier depth; smaller ones run faster. | Model | Repository | Parameters | Download size | |:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | S | [apple/DepthPro2-S](https://huggingface.co/apple/DepthPro2-S) | 24M | 97 MB | | B | [apple/DepthPro2-B](https://huggingface.co/apple/DepthPro2-B) | 97M | 386 MB | | L | [apple/DepthPro2-L](https://huggingface.co/apple/DepthPro2-L) | 334M | 1.3 GB | | H+ | [apple/DepthPro2-H](https://huggingface.co/apple/DepthPro2-H) | 872M | 3.5 GB | All sizes share a focal length estimator, [apple/DepthPro2-focal](https://huggingface.co/apple/DepthPro2-focal) (23.5M parameters, 94 MB), which loads with each size and predicts the focal length when it is unknown. ## Quick start ```bash pip install "git+https://github.com/apple-aiml-research/ml-depth-pro-2" ``` ```python from functools import partial import torch from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download from safetensors.torch import load_file from depth_pro_2 import DepthPro2, load_rgb, upright from depth_pro_2.model import to_normalized_tensor from depth_pro_2.network.fov import FOVEstimator # apple/DepthPro2-S, -B, -L or -H; bfloat16 is how the models run on a GPU. model = DepthPro2.from_pretrained("apple/DepthPro2-H", precision=torch.bfloat16) # The focal length estimator all sizes share, for photos and videos without a focal length. weights = hf_hub_download("apple/DepthPro2-focal", "model.safetensors") model.fov = FOVEstimator(torch.bfloat16) model.fov.load_state_dict(load_file(weights)) model = model.to("cuda").eval() transform = partial(to_normalized_tensor, device=torch.device("cuda")) ``` ### Image ```python # f_px is the focal length recorded in the photo, or None. image, f_px = load_rgb("photo.jpg") depth = model.infer(transform(image), f_px=f_px)["depth"] # meters, (H, W) ``` ### Video ```python import av # 16 frames at a time: one prediction per frame, in order. video = av.open("video.mp4") frames = (transform(upright(f)) for f in video.decode(video=0)) for prediction in model.infer_video(frames): depth = prediction["depth"] # meters, (H, W) ``` Depth is infinite where the scene is infinitely far, such as the sky. The [code](https://github.com/apple-aiml-research/ml-depth-pro-2) has the command line and a live-feed example. ## Results ### Sharpness and temporal consistency Depth Pro 2 outperforms prior work operating on a single frame or multiple frames on sharpness (Boundary F1 score) and temporal consistency (Jitter). Higher F1 and lower jitter are better, so the top right is best. Results averaged over Sintel and Spring datasets. ### Photos ![Depth Pro 2 on photos: the inputs on top, their predicted depth below](assets/teaser.jpg) Top row: the input photos. Bottom row: Depth Pro 2's depth, red near and blue far. ## Method A multi-view transformer processes one or more frames jointly, and a DPT decoder predicts an inverse depth map for each frame. ① After the first third of its blocks, th

--- library_name: transformers license: apache-2.0 pipeline_tag: image-text-to-text --- # Qwen3.8-27B > [!Note] > This repository contains model weights and configuration files for the post-trained model in the Hugging Face Transformers format. > > These artifacts are compatible with Hugging Face Transformers, vLLM, SGLang, TokenSpeed, etc. > [!Tip] > For users seeking managed, scalable inference without infrastructure maintenance, the official Qwen API service is provided by [Qwen Cloud](https://www.qwencloud.com). > In particular, **Qwen3.8-27B** will be available as a hosted version with more production features, e.g., 1M context length by default, official built-in tools. For more information, please refer to the [Qwen3.8-27B Overview](https://www.qwencloud.com/models/qwen3.8-27b). The service is coming soon. Stay tuned for updates. Following the widespread community adoption of the Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.6 series, we are pleased to introduce Qwen3.8, the most capable generation in the Qwen open-model family to date. Built on the architectural foundation of Qwen3.5, Qwen3.8 delivers substantial gains across coding, professional work, research, and long-horizon agentic tasks. Qwen3.8-27B brings these advances to a compact, deployment-friendly dense model: a native vision-language model that understands images and videos, with flexible thinking control, designed to carry complex, multi-step tasks through to completion with greater reliability. ## Qwen3.8 Highlights Qwen3.8-27B features the following enhancements: - **Core Capabilities**: Comprehensive improvements across coding, professional work, research, and long-horizon agentic tasks. - **Agent Execution**: Stronger autonomous planning and better handling of environment feedback, leading to more reliable end-to-end task completion. - **Downstream Compatibility**: Broader support for popular harnesses and development tools, making it easier to integrate into your existing stack. - **Flexible Thinking Control**: Thinking mode is on by default and can be disabled per request; reasoning depth can be tuned with `reasoning_effort`, and reasoning context from historical messages is retained via `preserve_thinking`. - **Vision-Language Understanding**: Native support for image and video understanding, from STEM diagrams and documents to hour-scale videos. ## Model Overview - Type: Causal Language Model with Vision Encoder - Training Stage: Pre-training & Post-training - Language Model - Number of Parameters: 27B - Hidden Dimension: 5120 - Token Embedding: 248,320 (Padded) - Number of Layers: 64 - Hidden Layout: 16 × (3 × (Gated DeltaNet → FFN) → 1 × (Gated Attention → FFN)) - Gated DeltaNet: - Number of Linear Attention Heads: 48 for V and 16 for QK - Head Dimension: 128 - Gated Attention: - Number of Attention Heads: 24 for Q and 4 for KV - Head Dimension: 256 - Rotary Position Embedding Dimension: 64 - Feed Forward Network: - Intermediate Dimension: 17,408 - LM Output: 248,320 (Padded) - MTP (Multi-Token Prediction): trained with multiple steps - Context Length: 262,144 natively and extensible up to 1,000,000 tokens. ## Benchmark Results ### Text Performance

English | 简体中文

## 🌐 Architecture ![这张图是SenseNova-Loop-9B的整体架构示意图，整体以淡紫色调呈现。图的上部展示模型的宏观层级流转：先经过前置循环的A层，随后进入标注为Looped block的循环模块，该模块包含1-st Looped Pass等多轮循环传递，每轮均包含多个TBK单元，对应模型中部的B层，之后进入后置循环的最后C层，最终接入LM Head得到输出。图的下部为mHC模块的内部细节，展示了特征通过Transform分支的Attention/FFN计算、结合双随机矩阵的残差混合多流操作，完成特征的迭代更新，直观呈现该模型的核心特殊架构设计。](assets/hero.png) ## 📣 News **🔥 2026-11-18:** Added download links for the [AWQ](https://huggingface.co/sensenova/SenseNova-Loop-9B-AWQ) and [GGUF](https://huggingface.co/sensenova/SenseNova-Loop-9B-GGUF) weights. **🔥 2026-11-17:** We release SenseNova-Loop-9B, with model weights and code available to the community. **🔥 2026-10-31:** We release SenseNova-Loop-9B-Preview, with model weights and code available to the community. ## 🚀 SenseNova-Loop-9B: Deeper Computation with Fewer Parameters We officially release SenseNova-Loop-9B. Building on the Preview's exploration of parameter efficiency, the model reuses layer weights through a looped architecture and combines them with manifold-constrained hyper-connections (mHC) to expand computational depth within a compact parameter budget. It is designed for complex reasoning, coding, tool use, and multimodal tasks. Since the Preview release, we have received community interest and feedback on model use, inference deployment, and ecosystem integration. The official release retains the looped architecture and two-stream mHC, further improving performance on agentic, coding, and data analysis tasks while continuing to explore the capabilities of looped computation. SenseNova-Loop-9B has approximately 9B parameters. By repeatedly executing shared middle layers, it extends 32 physical decoder layers into 56 layer executions. The model accepts text and images and generates text, supporting long-context understanding and multi-step tasks. In agentic and data analysis evaluations, the model is competitive with Qwen3.8-27B: it scores 41.36 versus 44.60 on NL2Repo and 65.31 versus 65.01 on AIDABench. ### Model Highlights - **Shared looped block:** 24 decoder layers are executed twice in sequence, producing 56 layer computations from 32 distinct layers per forward pass. - **Two-stream mHC:** learned mappings route and combine information between two residual streams within the looped block. - **Hybrid attention:** the decoder interleaves linear and full attention in a repeating four-layer pattern. - **Long-context multimodal training:** the training recipe includes text, images, code, and tool-use trajectories, with the context length extended to 512K tokens. - **Low-memory deployment:** With 4-bit weights and an 8-bit KV cache, multimodal inference at a 256K context length requires approximately 15 GiB of GPU memory. - **Official quantized release:** An official AWQ 4-bit version is available on launch day for easier deployment. ## 🎬 Showcase ### 3D ![Cloudside Market: rotating 3D scene](assets/showcase_ref_3d.gif) ### SVG + Web ![ORBIT: an interactive space exploration website](assets/showcase_ref_orbit.gif) ### Poster ![Distortion FM: an animated music festival poster](assets/showcase_ref_poster.gif) ### Web ![TYPE RELAY: an interactive typography exhibition](assets/showcase_ref_web.gif) ### Design ![Beyond the Coastline: a photo editorial website](assets/showcase_ref_coast.gif) ## 📊 Model Performance: From Preview to Release We evaluate SenseNova-Loop-9B on agentic, coding, and data analysis tasks, comparing the release with the Preview and other models. ![Benchmark comparison of SenseNova-Loop-9B, the Preview, and other models](assets/release_benchmark_iuua.png) The release outperforms the Preview on all seven benchmarks shown. AutomationBench rises from 14.33 to 36.67, Terminal-Bench 2.1 from 40.45 to 59.55, and GAIA from 37.86 to 69.90. Compared with Qwen3.8-27B, the release matches its 36.67 on AutomationBench and scores 65.31 versus 65.01 on AIDABench. On NL2Repo, it scores 41.36 versus 44.60. Its BIRD score of 72.34 is 0.96
